Subject: Scoped TIA & routing proposal — MedLogic pilot (SCCs / UK addendum options)

Hi Anna / MedLogic legal team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. As promised, attaching a lightweight Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) template that we typically use for pilot engagements. The goal for this thread is to: 1) confirm the scope of personal data flows for the pilot; 2) propose routing/hosting options that avoid unnecessary cross-border transfers; and 3) surface the subprocessor and contractual steps we need to finalize (SCCs + UK addendum / IDTA as appropriate).

High-level options for your review (we can pick one):
- Option A — EU-only processing: spin up a dedicated EU tenancy (EU KMS) and pin the pilot to an EU region. Minimal legal paperwork beyond SCCs; lowest transfer risk.
- Option B — Hybrid EU primary, UK fallback: primary processing in EU; UK fallback for low-latency UK users. Requires UK addendum + updated routing exceptions documented in the TIA.
- Option C — UK instance + UK IDTA: if majority of data subjects are UK residents or you require local residency, we can onboard a UK-dedicated instance and execute the UK IDTA (we can sign the addendum).

Immediate asks for you so we can scope the TIA:
1) A short list of pilot data types (PHI? pseudonymized ids? free text?).
2) Which jurisdictions the pilot will accept users from (EU only, EU+UK, global).
3) Any must-avoid subprocessors or sequencing constraints.

Attachments: MedLogic_TIA_Template.xlsx (TIA checklist + controls), redwood_subprocessor_snapshot_20280704.csv (current subprocessor snapshot), uk_addendum_draft_20280704.docx (draft addendum copy).

I can loop in Laura (Redwood legal) and Marcus (solutions) once you confirm the data picture — they can propose the compliance/redline approach and technical mitigations.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the summary and the templates — very helpful. A few clarifications from our side before we complete the TIA template: 

1) Data types: Pilot will include patient contact details (name, phone, email), appointment scheduling metadata, and short clinical notes (de-identified where possible but may contain free-text that could be sensitive). We consider the notes to be pseudonymized but not fully anonymized.

2) Jurisdictions: primary user base is Sweden + Norway; we expect a small number of UK users (~5% of traffic) but may expand.

3) Subprocessors: we have two redlines: (a) no routing to cloud provider X (we'll share the vendor list offline); (b) all logging/diagnostic exports must be retained in-region unless explicitly requested.

Specific question: for Option B (EU primary, UK fallback), will Redwood require us to sign both the SCCs and the UK addendum, or can the SCCs cover EU->UK transitions if we accept a routing exception? Also, do you have a current DTIAs (data transfer impact assessment) or evidence pack for your infra that we can reference?

If you can have Laura confirm the contractual approach and Marcus provide the technical isolation guarantees for Option A vs B, we can move quickly.

Best,
Anna Larsson
Head of Data Governance
MedLogic

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Scoped TIA & routing proposal — MedLogic pilot (SCCs / UK addendum options)

Anna — thanks for the rapid detail; this helps a lot. Short answers and next steps below.

Contractual posture:
- EU -> UK: The current supervisory guidance (and our legal view) is that transfers from EEA to UK require the UK addendum (IDTA / UK Addendum) in addition to the SCCs when the UK is treated as a third country under local frameworks. Practically, signing the SCCs plus the UK Addendum provides a clearer contractual basis for transfers that touch UK infrastructure.
- Routing exceptions: We can document routing exceptions in the TIA, but relying solely on SCCs w/o the UK Addendum leaves a residual risk vector for UK-specific rules. For a pilot with low UK volume, Option A (EU-only) is simplest. Option B is viable, but we'd expect MedLogic to sign the UK addendum before we allow automated fallback to UK processing.

DTIA / evidence pack:
- Attached to this message are two short artifacts: a one-page DTIA summary for our hosting regions and a snapshot of our subprocessor controls. These are redacted for public cloud provider names per our policy; we can provide full names under an NDA if needed.

Technical mitigations (high level):
- EU-only tenancy: we can provision an isolated project with EU KMS keys and region-locked logging; no egress outside EU unless requested.
- KV-cache routing: user prefixes can be pinned to EU hosts to reduce cross-region cache misses that would trigger fallback.
- Minimal UK fallback: if you need <10% UK traffic to be low-latency, we can enforce a policy that routes only hashed UK sessions to the UK instance; all diagnostics from UK nodes are retained in-region and only aggregated metrics cross borders.

Action items: 
- MedLogic: confirm whether clinical notes are treated as pseudonymized PHI (Anna) and share vendor blocklist.
- Redwood (Laura): prepare a redline of the UK addendum and share a redacted DTIA summary (attached).
- Redwood (Marcus): provide a one-page technical note on EU tenancy isolation and logging retention to include in the TIA.

Attachments referenced: redwood_DTIA_summary_20280706.pdf (redacted), redwood_subprocessor_controls_short.csv

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference
